title: Former Oracle engineer on H-1B visa shares how he's adapting to AI
excerpt: A former Oracle engineer says AI and layoffs have raised the stakes for H-1B visa holders. Here's how he's adapting.
content_html:
A former Oracle engineer on an H-1B visa says AI and tech layoffs pushed him into constant career-prep mode

By Jacob Zinkula

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

When Ayush Raj Jha moved from India to Illinois in 2018 to pursue a master's degree in computer science, he was optimistic about the future of software engineering.

Now, after years of layoffs and the rapid rise of AI, he's worried about the future of his industry — and his long-term future in the US.

Jha is one of hundreds of thousands of workers in the US on an H-1B visa, for whom losing a job can mean more than losing a paycheck. They generally have 60 days to find a new employer or risk losing their legal status in the US.

Major employers in tech rely heavily on H-1B workers. Federal data shows that the "Magnificent 7" companies, including the likes of Amazon and Apple, have had more than 200,000 H-1B applications approved since October 2020.

"It's really started impacting the lives of people who are on visas," Jha said. "There's constant fear and uncertainty."

He's among the tech workers who are looking for ways to stay competitive in an evolving industry. Some are responding by working harder and learning AI skills, while others are preparing for job searches or actively seeking more secure roles.

AI's impact on software engineering

After earning a master's degree from the Illinois Institute of Technology in 2020, Jha joined Motorola Solutions as a software engineer, where he worked on software for public safety agencies. In 2022, he joined Oracle as a senior software engineer, where he helped build cloud infrastructure used to deploy healthcare software to hospitals. ChatGPT was released late that year.

Since then, Jha said two things have reinforced his concerns about AI's impact on software engineering. The first is his experience using AI tools.

To stay competitive, Jha said he spends an estimated eight to 10 hours a week outside of work taking online courses on platforms like LinkedIn Learning and Coursera, experimenting with coding tools, and contributing to open-source projects. Seeing what the technology can do firsthand has both impressed and worried him, he said.

"If we don't adapt to these new technologies, it just becomes impossible to stay relevant or even be employable at this point," he said.

The second is LinkedIn. He said posts about tech layoffs have become a regular sight on his feed, serving as a constant reminder of how quickly the industry is changing.

Moving on from Oracle

Earlier this year, Jha started looking for a more senior, higher-paying role where he could make a bigger impact.

Layoffs at Oracle, most recently in March, had heightened his concerns about job security. While his primary focus was career advancement, he also hoped to find an employer that could offer greater stability, in part because of his visa status.

Jha said his job search was fairly challenging, which he expected given the hiring slowdown across parts of the tech sector. Eventually, he found a staff software engineer opening at a customer service software company that came with a higher title and pay than his position at Oracle.

The company's reputation for a strong engineering culture and ability to attract skilled professionals from diverse backgrounds was also a draw, Jha said. And it was privately owned, so Jha believed it might face less short-term pressure from market expectations, quarterly earnings, and shareholders — dynamics he hoped would make the role more secure than one at a public company.

Jha accepted an offer in July. Before starting with his new employer in September, Jha said he plans to take a roughly two-month career break while his H-1B transfer is finalized.

Advice for other engineers

Jha believes his more than a decade of experience as a software engineer helped him land his new role, but he also believes his online coursework and open-source contributions were important.

"I always try to stay up to date with market trends and emerging technologies rather than only focusing on day-to-day company work or simply building my resume," he said.

Jha said his advice to tech workers, regardless of their visa status, is to always be prepared to interview for their next job.

"At this point with AI adoption, it does not matter how well you perform even at your current company — you could be replaceable," he said.

科技行业的主要雇主严重依赖 H-1B 员工。 联邦数据显示，自 2020 年 10 月以来，包括亚马逊和苹果等在内的“Magnificent 7”公司已批准了超过 20 万份 H-1B 申请。

贾说：“这确实开始影响持签证人的生活。” “恐惧和不确定性一直存在。”

他是那些正在寻找在不断发展的行业中保持竞争力的方法的科技工作者之一。 一些人通过更加努力地工作和学习人工智能技能来应对，而另一些人则正在准备找工作或积极寻找更安全的职位。

人工智能对软件工程的影响

2020 年从伊利诺伊理工学院获得硕士学位后，Jha 加入摩托罗拉系统公司担任软件工程师，为公共安全机构开发软件。 2022 年，他加入 Oracle 担任高级软件工程师，帮助构建用于向医院部署医疗保健软件的云基础设施。 ChatGPT 于当年年底发布。

从那时起，贾说有两件事加强了他对人工智能对软件工程影响的担忧。 首先是他使用人工智能工具的经验。

Jha 表示，为了保持竞争力，他每周估计会在工作之余花费 8 到 10 个小时在 LinkedIn Learning 和 Coursera 等平台上学习在线课程，尝试编码工具，并为开源项目做出贡献。 他说，亲眼目睹这项技术的用途既让他印象深刻，又让他感到担忧。

“如果我们不适应这些新技术，目前就不可能保持相关性，甚至无法就业，”他说。

第二个是领英。 他表示，有关科技公司裁员的帖子已成为他的动态中经常出现的内容，不断提醒人们该行业正在快速变化。

离开甲骨文继续前进

今年早些时候，贾开始寻找更高级、薪水更高的职位，以便他能够产生更大的影响。

甲骨文公司的裁员（最近一次是在三月份）加剧了他对工作保障的担忧。 虽然他的主要关注点是职业发展，但他也希望找到一个能够提供更大稳定性的雇主，部分原因是他的签证身份。

贾哈表示，考虑到部分科技行业的招聘放缓，他的求职相当具有挑战性。 最终，他在一家客户服务软件公司找到了一名软件工程师，该公司的头衔和薪酬都比他在甲骨文的职位要高。

贾说，该公司以其强大的工程文化和吸引来自不同背景的熟练专业人士的能力而闻名，这也是一个吸引人的地方。 由于该公司是私营企业，因此贾认为，来自市场预期、季度收益和股东的短期压力可能会较小，他希望这些动态将使这一职位比上市公司的职位更加安全。

Jha 在七月份接受了一份工作邀请。 Jha 表示，在 9 月份开始与新雇主开始工作之前，他计划在 H-1B 调动完成期间进行大约两个月的职业休息。

给其他工程师的建议

Jha 认为，他十多年的软件工程师经验帮助他获得了新职位，但他也认为他的在线课程和开源贡献也很重要。

“我总是努力了解最新的市场趋势和新兴技术，而不是只专注于日常公司工作或仅仅构建我的简历，”他说。

贾说，他对科技工作者的建议是，无论他们的签证状态如何，都要时刻准备好面试下一份工作。

他说：“在人工智能被采用的这一点上，即使你在当前的公司表现得有多好，你也可能会被取代。”
